name: RUST-REF gcov dump — DUMP_COVERAGE walk of the instrumented twin (development evidence, never RfR)

image_version.reason: development dump plan on the instrumented twin; identity is recorded by dev-campaign (image sha256, toolchain), the pure RfR image is judged by the main plan

decision_log: 1. Author (2026-11-10, A19): one-test dump plan per fprime-system-test-harness §3a step 4 — run on the same twin build cache right after the coverage run of the main plan (never delete .gcda between them); the ground paces one DUMP_COVERAGE(start, 8) window per command until CoverageDumpDone; CoverageRejected == 0, no OpCodeError, no dropped events. Markers through rustTester.MARK like the main plan (each MARK also flushes the counters to disk, which is what the chunk-0 window then pages).

tests.title: Coverage dump walk
tests.purpose: Pages every gcov object of the twin out through rustTester.DUMP_COVERAGE so fth coverage-system can rebuild the .gcda files and measure the plan's system coverage.
tests.setup: Twin (FPRIME_RUST_REFERENCE_COVERAGE=ON) flashed from the same build cache the coverage run used; .gcda files of that run on disk.
procedure: DUMP_COVERAGE(start, 8) for start = 8, 16, ... paced, until CoverageDumpDone

rationale.text: stimulus-declared: fth 0.1.2's grammar has no >= on event counts, so the test declares `coverage dump done seen` via require/check on the live wait; the record carries the Done event(s) and fth coverage-system refuses a dump without exactly consistent Done/Object/Chunk rows

tests.evidence: CoverageDumpDone(objects, totalBytes, crc) at least once; no CoverageRejected; fth coverage-system reassembles N objects with the Done CRC.

ut.scope: what fth judges (T5): gcov/gcovr of the UUT's default-config fixture UT project lib/fprime-rust/tests/project via `fprime-util generate --ut && fprime-util check --all --coverage` (C++ fixtures ActiveFix/PassiveFix/QueuedFix exercising the generated shim and runtime glue, plus the F Prime config headers that project compiles). The Rust crates themselves are not gcov-instrumentable; cargo llvm-cov figures are reported informatively in dev-evidence, never judged against this threshold

system.scope: what fth judges (T5): the instrumented twin of FprimeRustReference (CMake option FPRIME_RUST_REFERENCE_COVERAGE=ON, GCC >= 12, separate build cache build-fprime-automatic-native-cov) runs the same plan on the native bench; counters are paged out by rustTester.DUMP_COVERAGE (gcov-dump plan) and measured by `fth coverage-system` with --filter FprimeRustReference/Components/ (hand-written Relay.cpp, RustTester.cpp), --filter lib/fprime-rust/FprimeRust/ (glue) and the twin-cache filter for the generated Rust shim RustCounter.cpp/RustMonitor.cpp with the FPP autocode *Ac.cpp excluded (regex build-fprime-automatic-native-cov/FprimeRustReference/Components/.*/(?!.*Ac\.cpp$)[^/]*\.cpp$) — FPP autocode is F Prime's, not the UUT's output. The pure RfR image is the OFF build; the Rust handler bodies are outside gcov's reach [I]

not_covered_ack: L3 reset/persistence across a process restart: the native bench defines no reset row (R7 names flash, dump, gds only); THRESHOLD persistence is proven by the saved file (L7-1), not by a reload
REQ-FprimeRust-024 panic-abort path: death test in UT only; never planted in the system run (it would end the record)
REQ-FprimeRust-017/-034/-035/-036 generation and build failure paths: autocoder/build UT only; the reference deployment models only supported elements

REQ-FprimeRust-030/-031/-032/-033 (parameterUpdated, internal ports, overflow hooks, port return values) and passive Rust components, guarded ports, sync/guarded commands, ACTIVITY_HI/COMMAND/DIAGNOSTIC/FATAL severities: shim UT only; the reference deployment exercises active + queued, async/sync members and three severities
coverage.rationale: UT baseline 95/85 from fprime-system-test-design; system 75 because the deployment's Svc/Drv framework code shares the executable and only the Rust integration surface is judged
